claims.quote: unemployed salesmen, waitresses, motel managers -- in the midst of disheartening lives. … They drop their characters back down where they find them, inarticulate and alone, drunk at noon.

claims.claim: 의자·포크 같은 평범한 사물과 무심해 보이는 대사 한 줄에 큰 힘을 싣는 글쓰기에 가장 관심이 있다고 스스로 썼다
claims.quote: to endow those things - a chair, a window curtain, a fork, a stone, a woman's earrings - with immense, even startling power. It is possible to write a line of seemingly innocuous dialogue and have it send a chill along the reader's spine - the source of artistic delight, as Nabokov would have it. That's the kind of writing that most interests me.

claims.claim: 긴장은 빠진 것과 암시된 것에서도 나온다고 스스로 썼다
claims.quote: What creates tension in a piece of fiction is partly the way the concrete words are linked together to make up the visible action of the story. But it's also the things that are left out, that are implied

claims.claim: 카버 자신이 설명과 결말을 덜어내는 글쓰기를 지향했다

claims.note: D. T. Max가 릴리 도서관 원고로 확인한 바 결말 삭제·개작은 리시의 손. 카버 스스로는 『파리 리뷰』에서 그 시기 '골수까지' 깎아냈다고 말했을 뿐 결말을 덜어내는 것을 지향했다고 말한 대목은 찾지 못함.

They drop their characters back down where they find them, inarticulate and alone, drunk at noon. The later two collections are fuller, touched by optimism, even sentimentality.

claims.quote:
발행일

claims.claim: 체호프에서 카버로 향하는 영향이 문헌(카버 본인의 발언)으로 확인된다
claims.quote: Chekhov. I suppose he's the writer whose work I most admire.

claims.claim: 인터뷰는 1983년 『파리 리뷰』의 「The Art of Fiction No. 76」이다
claims.quote:
Raymond Carver, The Art of Fiction No. 76 
 Interviewed by Mona Simpson, Lewis Buzbee 
 Issue 88, Summer 1983

claims.claim: 문학적 영향이나 존경하는 작가를 묻자 체호프를 작품을 가장 존경하는 작가로 꼽았다
claims.quote: Can you talk a little about literary influences, or at least name some writers whose work you greatly admire? … Chekhov. I suppose he's the writer whose work I most admire.

claims.claim: 대학 시절 읽은 체호프의 편지와 단편이 사물을 전과 다르게 보게 했다고 말했다
claims.quote: (Understand I was in college at the time and reading plays about princes and dukes and the overthrow of kingdoms. Quests and the like, large undertakings to establish heroes in their rightful places. Novels with larger-than-life heroes.) But reading what Chekhov had to say in that letter, and in other letters of his as well, and reading his stories, made me see things differently than I had before.

claims.claim: 「A Storyteller's Shoptalk」에 체호프 단편의 한 구절을 카드에 적어 책상 옆에 붙여 두었다고 썼다
claims.quote: Someday I'll put that on a three-by-five card and tape it to the wall beside my desk. I have some three-by-five cards on the wall now. … I have a three-by-five up there with this fragment of a sentence from a story by Chekhov

claims.claim: 이 에세이는 1981년 『뉴욕 타임스 북 리뷰』에 실렸다
claims.quote: Some months ago, in this Book Review, John Barth said

claims.claim: 1987년 체호프의 죽음을 다룬 단편 「심부름」을 썼다
claims.quote: He felt ''in the pink of health'' in 1987 when he wrote ''Errand,'' a story about Chekhov's death from tuberculosis.

claims.claim: 오코너에서 카버로 향하는 영향이 문헌(카버 본인의 글)으로 확인된다
claims.quote: I remember being tremendously heartened by reading what she had to say on the subject.

claims.claim: 「A Storyteller's Shoptalk」에서 오코너의 에세이 「Writing Short Stories」를 길게 인용했다
claims.quote: In an essay called, simply enough, ''Writing Short Stories,'' Flannery O'Connor talks about writing as an act of discovery. … She uses ''Good Country People'' as an example of how she put together a short story whose ending she could not even guess at until she was nearly there:

claims.claim: 결말을 모른 채 쓰기 시작한다는 오코너의 말을 읽고 크게 용기를 얻었다고 썼다
claims.quote: O'Connor says she most often did not know where she was going when she sat down to work on a short story. … I remember being tremendously heartened by reading what she had to say on the subject.

claims.claim: 첫 문장 하나만 가지고 앉아 시를 쓰듯 한 줄씩 이어 단편을 완성한 경험을 적었다
claims.quote: I did, and I sat down in the morning and wrote the first sentence, and other sentences promptly began to attach themselves. I made the story just as I'd make a poem; one line and then the next, and the next.

claims.claim: 1983년 『파리 리뷰』 인터뷰에서 존경하는 작가로 오코너를 꼽았다
claims.quote: Isaac Babel, Flannery O'Connor, Frank O'Connor. James Joyce's Dubliners .
